userStories.title: Pure Kahn topo-sort + WSJF ranking module (src/issues/rank.ts)
userStories.description: As the cam triage core, I need a pure ranking function that computes a dense 1-based rank over the {stage:specified, status:open} set via Kahn layers ordered by WSJF, so that nothing is ranked before its blocker and high-value-low-effort issues win within an unblocked layer.
acceptanceCriteria: A pure ranking function in src/issues/rank.ts computes a dense 1-based rank over the {stage:specified,status:open} set: Kahn layers over blockedBy edges internal to the set (shipped blockers treated as satisfied and ignored), within each in-degree-zero layer sorted by WSJF descending then numeric id ascending. [oracle: bun test (unit tests for layering, WSJF order, id tie-break)]

WSJF equals (value plus timeCriticality plus riskReduction) divided by jobSize; a specified issue with missing wsjf or jobSize less-than-or-equal-0 is treated as WSJF 0 (sorts last in its layer) with a warning, never a crash or divide-by-zero. [oracle: bun test (missing-wsjf and jobSize-0 cases assert WSJF 0 plus warn, no throw)]
Numeric id tie-break matches selectPlannableIssue's numericIdSuffix semantics (numeric suffix ascending, e.g. CAM-9 before CAM-12). [oracle: bun test (id tie-break ordering)]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: File: NEW src/issues/rank.ts. Pure function over IssueEntry[] (src/issues/types.ts): WsjfScore {value,timeCriticality,riskReduction,jobSize}, IssueEntry.blockedBy[]/rank?/stage/status. Universe = {stage:'specified', status:'open'}; idea/shipped/abandoned excluded; 'planned' is defined-but-unreachable today (ignore it -- nothing sets it). Kahn HAND-ROLLED (zero extra dependency, cam ethos): build in-degree over blockedBy edges that point INTO the set; a blockedBy id whose target is stage:'shipped' (or outside the set entirely -- see US-003 cross-stage handling) is a satisfied edge that does not contribute in-degree. Within each in-degree-zero layer: sort WSJF desc, tie-break numeric id asc. Dense 1-based rank assigned in emission order across layers. WSJF = (value+timeCriticality+riskReduction)/jobSize; missing wsjf OR jobSize<=0 => WSJF 0 + push a warning string (return warnings array, do not console.log from the pure fn). Return shape suggestion: { ranked: Array<{id, rank, wsjf, stage}>, warnings: string[] } -- caller (US-004) prints/commits. Mirror select.ts numericIdSuffix (src/issues/select.ts:9-14) for the tie-break: numeric suffix asc, non-parseable => Infinity (sorts last). GOTCHAS: pure/injectable/hermetic (no shelling out, no fs); never divide-by-zero; this is the FIRST writer-side computation of rank (select.ts only reads rank). Cycle detection lives in US-003, not here -- but expose enough structure (e.g. the residual non-zero in-degree set) for US-003's gate to name the cycle. Maps spec AC#1, AC#2.

userStories.title: Graph gate: Kahn cycle detection + referential-integrity reuse
userStories.description: As the cam triage safety net, I need a deterministic graph gate that hard-fails transactionally (no rank written) on a cycle, a missing-id, or a self-reference, naming the offending path/edge, while a cross-stage blocker only warns, so that a bad graph never silently corrupts the rank.
acceptanceCriteria: Kahn detects a cycle (nodes whose in-degree never reaches zero); the gate hard-fails, names the cycle path (e.g. CAM-X to CAM-Y to CAM-X), writes NO rank, and reports a non-zero/fail result. [oracle: bun test (cyclic graph rejected, ranks unchanged) plus file-assert the cycle ids appear in the error]

The gate reuses checkReferentialIntegrity (src/issues/graph.ts) to hard-fail on a blockedBy pointing to a non-existent id or a self-reference, transactionally (no rank written), naming the offending edge. [oracle: bun test (missing-id and self-ref each rejected with no write)]

A specified issue blockedBy an idea, abandoned, or otherwise non-shipped-non-specified id is ranked by its intra-set position and emits a warning, not a hard fail. [oracle: bun test (cross-stage blocker ranked plus warning, exit 0)]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: File: extend src/issues/rank.ts (or NEW src/issues/gate.ts that composes rank.ts + graph.ts). REUSE src/issues/graph.ts -- it ALREADY has checkReferentialIntegrity (graph.ts:49, flags missing-id + self-ref) and deriveBlocks (graph.ts:23); graph.ts:47 EXPLICITLY defers full cycle-rejection to THIS issue. Do NOT reinvent missing-id/self-ref -- call checkReferentialIntegrity. ADD only Kahn cycle detection: after Kahn drains all in-degree-zero layers, any node with residual non-zero in-degree is on a cycle; reconstruct and name the cycle path (CAM-X -> CAM-Y -> CAM-X) by walking blockedBy among the residual set. Gate return shape: { ok: true } | { ok: false, kind: 'cycle'|'integrity', errors: string[] }. TRANSACTIONAL: the gate runs and must pass BEFORE any rank is computed-for-write/committed; on fail, prior ranks are kept untouched (the gate is a pure check; the no-write guarantee is enforced by US-004 calling the gate before the commit). CROSS-STAGE blocker (specified issue blockedBy an idea/abandoned/non-shipped-non-specified id that IS present in the backlog) is NOT an integrity error and NOT a cycle: it is a satisfied/ignored edge for intra-set Kahn (the blocker is outside {specified,open}) and emits a WARNING, exit 0. Distinguish: missing-id (not in backlog at all) = hard fail via checkReferentialIntegrity; present-but-out-of-set = warn. GOTCHAS: blocks is derived (deriveBlocks), never stored, single-direction (blockedBy is the source of truth). Maps spec AC#3, AC#4, AC#5.

userStories.title: `cam triage` deterministic CLI writing rank to main
userStories.description: As an operator, I need a deterministic `cam triage` command that reads {specified,open} from main, computes ranks, runs the gate, and on pass writes rank to every such issue and commits to main via the shared helper (never touching the work branch), printing the ranked order, the diff vs prior, warnings, and a machine sentinel, so that the backlog is reprioritized deterministically and idempotently.
acceptanceCriteria: cam triage runs the gate BEFORE any write and, on gate pass, writes the computed rank onto every {specified,open} issue all-ranks-or-none; the gate-before-write ordering and the rank write are verified in-process with an injected spawnFn (no real git). [oracle: bun test with injected spawnFn asserts gate-runs-before-any-write ordering + rank written to the serialized issues.local.json payload]

When computed ranks equal current ranks, cam triage performs no write and creates no commit (idempotent no-op), verified in-process with an injected spawnFn. [oracle: bun test asserts a second run with unchanged ranks performs no write/commit (no commit-tree/update-ref spawn call)]

cam triage prints the resulting ranked order (id, rank, WSJF, stage) plus a diff versus prior rank (up, down, new, unchanged) and any warnings, and emits CAM_TRIAGE_RANKED=<n> changed=<m> sha=<commit-or-none> on success or CAM_TRIAGE_REJECTED=cycle:... on hard-fail. [oracle: file-assert grep the sentinel lines in a captured-stdout test]

On gate hard-fail (cycle or integrity), cam triage keeps prior ranks, writes no commit, prints CAM_TRIAGE_REJECTED=cycle:..., and exits non-zero. [oracle: bun test (gate-fail path writes no commit, exit 1, sentinel present)]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Files: NEW src/commands/triage.ts; wire dispatch in index.ts. cam triage is a DETERMINISTIC CLI (family: cam issue --file-local, cam journal append, cam ship --finalize), NOT a thin-proxy into the orchestrator pane -- it runs in-process and commits to main directly. Mirror src/commands/ship-finalize.ts / issue-file.ts shape (injectable SpawnFn + clock + readers; exported result interface). Flow: (1) read backlog from main via `git show main:scripts/cam/issues.local.json` (same as issue-file.ts:396), never the working tree; (2) run the US-003 gate; on fail print CAM_TRIAGE_REJECTED=cycle:<path> (or integrity), keep prior ranks, exit 1; (3) on pass compute dense ranks (US-002) for the {specified,open} set; (4) build diff vs each issue's prior rank (up/down/new/unchanged); (5) if NO rank changed => no-op: print no-change line + CAM_TRIAGE_RANKED=<n> changed=0 sha=none, skip the commit (NO empty commit); (6) else write rank onto every {specified,open} entry, serialize JSON.stringify(data,null,2)+'\n', commit to main via the US-001 shared helper (off-main commit-tree when on a work branch; on-main direct commit when branchWasMain), print ranked order (id,rank,WSJF,stage) + diff + warnings + CAM_TRIAGE_RANKED=<n> changed=<m> sha=<short>. VERIFICATION SPLIT: US-004 is fully verifiable IN-PROCESS (injected spawnFn / fake repo) -- AC#1/AC#2 assert gate-before-write ordering and idempotent no-op via the injected spawn call sequence. The REAL-git end-to-end proof (rank lands on main, work-branch HEAD unchanged, real second-run no-op) is owned EXCLUSIVELY by US-005; do NOT add a real-git test here.
